title: Missing Reinspection Record for Transmission Structure with Conflicting System Evidence
scenario_text:
Context from IBM Maximo (Asset #TL-4472-019, Transmission Structure 19, Line 4472):
Asset class: Steel lattice tower | Install date: 1978 | Last PM: 2018-06-14 (climbing inspection) | Condition: B2 (Fair) | Next scheduled: 2023-06-14 | Status: OVERDUE | No attached work orders after 2018.

Context from scanned paper logbook (PDF, 2012-09-22, Crew Lead: Mike Trujillo — retired 2016):
Page scan reads: 'Structure 19 — 4472. Section loss observed bottom gusset plate NE leg, approx 15% remaining cross-section. CP readings below threshold. Recommend reinspection 5 yr max per NESC Rule 214A1. Notified Brennan.'

Context from SharePoint — /engineering/inspection-reports/2017/ (folder listing):
Files present: TL-4472-Str14-17.pdf, TL-4472-Str15-17.pdf, TL-4472-Str18-17.pdf, TL-4472-Str20-17.pdf. No file for Structure 19.

Context from SAP PM (Work Order history for Functional Location TL-4472):
WO 400182 (2017-04-10): 'Climbing inspection — Structures 14-20, Line 4472' | Status: TECO | Actual hours: 42 | Settlement: Cost center 55100 (O&M).

Context from Microsoft Teams — #asset-integrity (2023-08-14, 2:43 PM):
@dave.kowalski: Doug, the PUC data request for aging infrastructure — they want reinspection compliance for all lines with structures older than 1985. Line 4472 is on the list. Are we good?
@doug.brennan: Let me check. Should be — we did the full line in 2017.
@dave.kowalski: (thumbs up emoji)
[No further messages in thread]

Context from Esri ArcGIS (Asset layer, queried today):
TL-4472-019 | Last inspection attribute: 2017-04-10 | Inspector: R. Garza | Condition code: B2 | Flag: none.

Context from GIS edit history (metadata):
TL-4472-019 inspection date field last modified: 2018-07-02 by user 'system_batch_upload' | Prior value: 2012-09-22.
question: The PUC has requested documentation proving Structure 19 on Line 4472 received its mandated 5-year reinspection after the 2012 finding. Based on all available evidence, what is the most defensible conclusion about whether the reinspection occurred?

contributor.name: Douglas Brennan
contributor.title: Asset Integrity Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Infrastructure inspection programs, regulatory compliance for aging assets, condition-based maintenance

choices: The reinspection likely occurred in 2017 (WO 400182 covered Structures 14-20) but there is no individual structure report for Str 19 in SharePoint, and the GIS date was set by a batch upload — the evidence is insufficient to demonstrate compliance to the PUC.
The reinspection was completed in 2017 as part of WO 400182; the GIS attribute confirms it; the company is in compliance.
The reinspection did not occur; the missing SharePoint report and the Maximo 2018 entry (not 2017) prove the 2017 work order skipped Structure 19.
The 2018 Maximo climbing inspection satisfies the 5-year reinspection requirement from the 2012 finding, making the 2017 question moot.
